passage: In the school garden club, Samir's chilli plant was drooping. 'Give it fertiliser,' said an older boy. Samir had none. He thought: what does a plant really need? He counted on his fingers: water, light, soil. Light first. The pot sat by the sunny window, so that was fine. Soil next: dark and loose, fine. Water last: the soil was soggy and smelled sour. He lifted the pot and looked underneath. No hole. The water had nowhere to go. He told Preeti Ma'am, the club teacher, who helped him move the plant to a pot with holes in the bottom. Two days later the leaves were lifting.

I'm Samir, and I sit next to Chetan in class, so I saw the tulsi saga.
His tulsi plant was drooping. His uncle said to buy fertiliser. Chetan didn't. He went to the library and read about what a plant needs to live. He came back with a list: water, light, soil. "If those three are fine, it should be fine," he told me.
Light: the plant sits on a sunny window, fine. Water: a glass every morning. Soil: he poked it and it was soggy, like mud.
Then he lifted the pot. There was no hole at the bottom. The water had nowhere to go.
He drilled a hole with his compass. Two weeks later the tulsi was standing straight. I don't know if he was proud, but he kept showing it to everybody.

qa.q: What did Chetan drill the hole with?
qa.a: He drilled a hole with his compass.

qa.q: What might Chetan showing the plant to everybody suggest?
qa.a: It suggests Chetan felt proud and pleased that working it out himself saved the plant, though Samir can't know for sure.

qa.q: What else could Chetan have done if water, light and soil all looked fine?
qa.a: He could ask a gardener or teacher about pests or the pot size, adding the next basic need to check.

qa.q: How might Chetan's uncle see the result?
qa.a: The uncle may be surprised that the fix was a drainage hole, not fertiliser, and could be impressed by Chetan's thinking.

Monday. Yusuf's money plant had yellow leaves. His neighbour Sachin said, "Put fertiliser, that's what my mother does."
Yusuf said, "But why is it yellow? What does a plant even need?"
Wednesday. In a library book, Yusuf read that plants need water, light and soil with air in it. He made three boxes in his notebook. Light, yes, near a window. Water, yes, daily. Soil... he pushed his finger in. Wet and smelly.
Friday. He turned the pot upside down over the sink. No drainage hole at all. His father helped him move the plant into an old paint tin with holes punched in the bottom.
Two weeks later the new leaves were green. Sachin said, "So no fertiliser?"
"It needed a hole, not medicine," Yusuf said.

qa.q: What did Yusuf's father help him move the plant into?
qa.a: An old paint tin with holes punched in the bottom.

qa.q: What was Yusuf wondering when Sachin suggested fertiliser?
qa.a: He was curious and doubtful, wanting to know why the leaves were yellow before adding anything.

qa.q: What else could Yusuf do so the plant stays healthy?
qa.a: He could check the soil with his finger before watering, so the new pot doesn't get soggy too.

qa.q: How might Sachin see Yusuf's way of solving it?
qa.a: Sachin may be surprised that the answer was a hole and not fertiliser, and may start asking why before copying what others do.

grounding: It shows a boy asking what plants really need, checking water, light and soil, and finding the pot has no drainage.
